query: A 70-year-old male with chronic heart failure and an ejection fraction of 30% develops a wide-complex tachycardia at 180 bpm. He is hemodynamically unstable. What is the immediate management?

A 63-year-old male with hypertension and type 2 diabetes undergoes carotid ultrasound that shows 75% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery. He is asymptomatic. What are the criteria for carotid endarterectomy versus medical management?

A 70-year-old male with type 2 diabetes on sulfonylurea is brought in unresponsive with a blood glucose of 28 mg/dL. He lives alone. What is the acute treatment and what long-term medication adjustment is required?

A 16-year-old female presents with primary amenorrhea, absent breast development, and blind-ending vagina. Karyotype is 46,XY. Testosterone levels are in the normal male range. What is the diagnosis?

A 35-year-old female presents with oligomenorrhea, acne, hirsutism, and a fasting insulin of 28 mIU/L. Pelvic ultrasound reveals bilateral polycystic ovaries. She is trying to conceive. What are the first-line treatments for ovulation induction?

A 70-year-old male presents with fatigue, reduced libido, and erectile dysfunction. Total testosterone is 7.2 nmol/L on two morning samples. LH and FSH are both low. Pituitary MRI reveals a 6 mm microadenoma. What is the hormonal diagnosis and management sequence?

A 68-year-old female with a three-year history of type 2 diabetes and eGFR of 35 mL/min presents for review. Her current metformin dose is 1000 mg twice daily. What medication adjustments are required and what agents are preferred for glycaemic control at this renal function?

A 52-year-old female presents with fatigue, myalgia, and constipation. Serum calcium is 11.8 mg/dL and PTH is 110 pg/mL. A sestamibi scan reveals a hot spot posterior to the inferior right thyroid pole. What is the diagnosis and when is surgery indicated?

A 50-year-old male presents with recurrent episodes of confusion and sweating, typically occurring in the late afternoon. What is the next step in evaluating for an endogenous hyperinsulinemic state?

Low-dose dexamethasone suppression fails to suppress cortisol, but high-dose suppression achieves > 50% reduction. What is the most likely source?
